The vertex shader computes the voxel index for each vertex $vp$ with color $vc$ [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Algorithm 4 (Voxelization: Vertex Shader) that the shader takes 'vp {Vertex 3D Position}' and 'vc {Vertex Color (RGB)}' as inputs. The claim accurately reflects that the vertex shader computes the voxel index for each vertex.

The approach differs from earlier methods by Karabassi et al. and Passalis et al., which used six z-buffers and six passes, by utilizing a single render pass and buffer [S1].

The claim states that the approach differs from earlier methods by Karabassi et al. and Passalis et al. by using a single render pass and buffer instead of six z-buffers and six passes. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in multiple locations: 1) The notes section states: 'Unlike Karabassi et al. [9] and Passalis et al. [12] which use six z-buffers and six passes, this approach uses a single render pass and a single buffer while keeping original voxel color.' 2) The passages section states: 'Our voxelization method has some similarities to the one developed by Karabassi et al. [9] and Passalis et al. [12], but while they use six z-buffers and thus six passes, our point-based approach uses only one render pass, and therefore uses a single buffer while keeping the original voxel color.' 3) Another passage reiterates: 'unlike the method developed by Karabassi et al. [9] which renders the surface six times, we use a single frame buffer and only one rasterization is needed'. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

Image-space voxelization projects the vertices of a triangular mesh into a 2D image stored in a Frame Buffer Object (FBO) to determine voxel locations and colors [S1].

The claim states that image-space voxelization projects vertices of a triangular mesh into a 2D image stored in a Frame Buffer Object (FBO) to determine voxel locations and colors. It further details that the FBO stores vertex color in RGB channels and voxel information in the alpha channel, which aligns with the claim's assertion about determining voxel locations and colors.
